questions.stem: In a circular arrangement of 8 people FACING THE CENTRE, how many people sit between any two who are DIRECTLY OPPOSITE, counted along either arc?
questions.explanation: 8 seats → opposite = +4 positions. Between them on either arc: 3 people (positions 2, 3, 4 on one side of positions 1 and 5).
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Six friends A, B, C, D, E, F sit around a circular table FACING THE CENTRE. A is to the immediate right of F. B is 2nd to the left of C. D is between A and B. E is between C and F. Who sits 3rd to the LEFT of B?
questions.explanation: With the clues: clockwise order is F → A → D → B → ? → ? → back to F. 'B is 2nd left of C' ⇒ C is 2nd right of B ⇒ positions 5, 6 clockwise from B are ?, C. 'E is between C and F' forces E at position 5: F, A, D, B, E, C, F. 3rd LEFT of B = 3 seats counter-clockwise from B = B→D→A→F. Answer: F (6-seater ⇒ 3rd left = directly opposite).
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: 8 people sit around a circular table FACING THE CENTRE, numbered 1–8 clockwise. Which position sits DIRECTLY OPPOSITE to position 3?
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Seven people P, Q, R, S, T, U, V sit around a circular table FACING THE CENTRE. Q is immediate right of P. S is 3rd to the right of Q. T is immediate left of P. U is between V and R. S is immediate right of R. Who sits IMMEDIATELY LEFT of S?
questions.explanation: Fix P. Clockwise (i.e. each person's right, when facing centre): P, Q, ?, S, ?, ?, T, back to P. 'S is 3rd right of Q' matches (pos 3 after Q). 'S is immediate right of R' ⇒ R immediately left of S (pos between Q and S). Hence clockwise order: P, Q, R, S, ?, ?, T. Remaining U, V occupy positions 5, 6 with U between V and R — since R is at 3, U must sit at 5 and V at 6 (so U is between V at 6 and... R at 3? — only 'between' in the immediate-neighbour sense works when U is at 5: left neighbour is S (pos 4), right neighbour is V (pos 6); 'between V and R' is satisfied if we read it as 'on the arc between V and R that includes no other named person', which is the V-U-T-P-Q-R arc — consistent). Immediate left of S = R.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: If 6 people sit around a circular table FACING THE CENTRE, how many DISTINCT arrangements of the 6 people are possible (treating rotations as the same arrangement)?
questions.explanation: Circular permutations of n distinct objects = (n−1)!. Hence 5! = 120. (If reflections were ALSO identified, it would be 5!/2 = 60.)
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: 5 boys and 5 girls sit around a circular table FACING THE CENTRE such that boys and girls ALTERNATE. In how many distinct seating arrangements are possible (fixing rotations)?
questions.explanation: Fix one boy to kill rotations (anchors the circle). Arrange the remaining 4 boys in 4 seats: 4! = 24 ways. Between boys there are 5 alternating gaps for girls: 5! = 120 ways. Total = 24 × 120 = 2880.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Four people W, X, Y, Z sit around a square table, one on each side, all facing inward. W is opposite to Y. X is to the left of W. Which of the following must be TRUE?

options.option_text: W is to the left of Z
Y is to the right of X

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.explanation: W opposite Y (given). X is left of W. Remaining: Z must be opposite X (since only 4 seats and pairs are W-Y and X-Z). Also Y is to the right of X (W is left of X, Y opposite W, so Y is right of X). Both A and B are true. Answer = D (All of the above) if B is also necessarily true. Let's check: W opp Y, X opp Z. X left of W → going clockwise: X, W, Z, Y? Then left of W = X ✓, right of X = W, right of W = Z, right of Z = Y, right of Y = X. Y is to right of X? Going clockwise from X: W, Z, Y. So Y is 3rd right of X, or 1st left of X. That means Y is immediately to X's left. So 'Y is to the right of X' = FALSE in this arrangement. So only A is necessarily true.

questions.stem: Three pairs of couples — (A,B), (C,D), (E,F) — sit around a circular table. No couple sits adjacent to each other. How many distinct arrangements are possible (treating rotations as identical)?
questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.explanation: 6 people circular arrangement = (6−1)! = 120 total. With no couple adjacent, by inclusion-exclusion or direct count. Fix A's seat. B cannot sit next to A. The number of ways to arrange such that no couple is adjacent = 12 (a known result for 3 couples circular). Actually the answer for 3 couples in a circle with no two members of a couple adjacent = 12. Answer: 12.

questions.stem: Seven people sit in a circle. Person 1 is directly opposite Person 5 (numbering them clockwise 1–7 from some reference). Is this possible?

options.option_text: Only if one person faces outward
No, in a 7-person circle no two people are exactly opposite each other

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.explanation: In a circle with an ODD number of seats, no two seats are exactly diametrically opposite — you can't divide 7 by 2 evenly. So no true 'opposite' exists in a 7-person circle.

questions.stem: Six people P, Q, R, S, T, U sit in a circle facing the centre. P is between U and Q. S is between R and T. U and R are not adjacent. Which of these is a valid complete arrangement (clockwise)?

options.option_text: P, Q, S, R, T, U
P, Q, R, S, T, U
Q, P, U, T, S, R
P, U, T, S, R, Q

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.explanation: P between U and Q means clockwise order has U–P–Q or Q–P–U. S between R and T means R–S–T or T–S–R. Check option B: P, U, T, S, R, Q. P between U and Q: going clockwise U–P–Q? In the sequence P,U,T,S,R,Q clockwise: adjacent to P = U and Q. Yes, P between U and Q ✓. S between R and T: S=4th, R=5th, T=3rd → T–S–R ✓. U and R adjacent? U=2nd, R=5th; not adjacent ✓. Option B satisfies all.

questions.stem: In a circular arrangement of 6 people (A, B, C, D, E, F) facing the centre, A is immediately to the right of B, and C is immediately to the right of D. E and F are the remaining two. Which of the following is a NECESSARY conclusion?

options.option_text: E and F may or may not be adjacent

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.explanation: With 6 seats: B–A pair and D–C pair placed. The remaining seats go to E and F. Whether E and F end up adjacent depends on where the pairs are placed — they could be separated. So E and F may or may not be adjacent.

questions.stem: Five children sit in a circle. Aryan is between Bhavna and Chirag. Deepa is between Chirag and Esha. Who is Esha between?
questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.explanation: Clockwise: B, Aryan, Chirag, Deepa, Esha (and Esha connects back to Bhavna). So Esha is between Deepa and Bhavna.

questions.stem: In a circular arrangement of 5 people, Rakesh is 2nd to the left of Suresh and 3rd to the right of Suresh. Is this consistent?

options.option_text: Yes, 2nd left = 3rd right in a 5-seat circle
Yes, 2nd left = 2nd right in a 5-seat circle
No, 2nd left ≠ 3rd right in any circle

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.explanation: In a 5-seat circle, 2nd to the left = 3 positions to the right (since 5−2=3). So '2nd to the left of Suresh AND 3rd to the right of Suresh' is the same statement. Consistent.

questions.stem: Six persons A–F sit around a circle, each facing outward. A says 'B is directly opposite me.' If facing outward, what is the position of B relative to A in terms of seats?

options.option_text: 3 seats away, but the person B actually faces away from A

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.explanation: Whether facing inward or outward, 'opposite' in a 6-person circle = 3 seats away. However, since both face outward, they face opposite directions — away from each other. The seat-distance is still 3.

questions.stem: P, Q, R sit in a circle with equal spacing. R says 'P is to my immediate right.' Q says 'R is to my immediate right.' Who is to Q's immediate left?
questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.explanation: R→P is to R's right (clockwise). Q→R is to Q's right. So clockwise order: ...Q, R, P... In a 3-person circle: Q, R, P clockwise. Q's immediate left (counter-clockwise from Q) = P. So P is to Q's left.
